title: M1: Batch runner — compile and run Python, C, and C++ projects
description: Intent: As the student, I want to submit a small multi-file project and get compiler output, program output, exit status, and timing back, so that I can run real code. Includes: runner container image (gcc, g++, python3), Node runner server, multi-file projects, stdin supplied up front, wall-clock and memory limits, output-size caps. Excludes: live interactive stdin, cloud deployment, UI. Definition of Done: all M1 stories' Gherkin specs pass against the runner in a local container.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Starting M1. Plan: runner workspace with a Node library (runProject) plus a small HTTP server (POST /run); executable Gherkin first, against a real local gcc/g++/python3 and then the Docker image. Cloud and interactivity are later milestones.

right_now_summary: Work is starting on a local runner for multi-file Python, C, and C++ projects.
